text.p: British car components, helicopters and armoured vehicles group GKN Plc is believed to be stalking Vickers Plc, maker of Challenger tanks and Rolls-Royce cars, said The Sunday Times.
The paper said analysts and investment bankers thought a bid was possible, although GKN "might prefer to wait and see whether Vickers' price falls further".

Last week Vickers' share price fell on a profit warning for the first six months of 1997, with chairman Sir Richard Lloyd telling the annual meeting that the strength of sterling was making exports difficult and putting pressure on profit margins.

"GKN last year dismissed rumours that it might bid for Vickers as 'a flight of fancy'," The Sunday Times said. But it said Vickers shares, which then stood around 270 pence, had fallen since. They closed at 207 pence on Friday, valuing the company at 698 million pounds ($1.1 billion).
Vickers has long said there needed to be consolidation of Europe's armoured vehicles industry and GKN has long been seen as a potential predator.

GKN makes Warrior, Saxon and Piranha armoured vehicles and was likely to break up the Vickers group if it got its hands on it, selling off the cars and medical equipment divisions to other companies, the report said.

"With Warrior orders running out later this year, GKN faces big costs for cutting back its Telford (northwest England) armoured-vehicles factory," The Sunday Times said. "By contrast, a British Army order for Challenger 2 tanks runs until 2000 and Vickers is pushing hard for tank export orders."
